hero.rubrik: $199 is for the shortest cover. Here is the price for your length, and a straight answer to everything else you asked.
hero.ingress: More than a hundred of you have left comments on the ads, and the same questions come back every day. Does it fit a 32-footer? What about the A/C unit on the roof? Are those straps going to hold? This page answers them in order. Where we don't know yet, it says so instead of guessing.
hero.knapp: See all nine sizes and prices → from $199
sammanfattning: The cover comes in nine lengths, 18 to 44 ft, all 10 ft wide, from $199 to $389. The full price list is right below, with a button for each length that opens that size on the product page.

After the table come the seven things RV owners ask most, in order: your length and price, the rooftop A/C, the straps, moisture under the cover, why not a full-body cover, fifth wheels and the rest of what sits on your roof, and what you get if it doesn't fit. Where the maker hasn't answered yet, it says 'we asked' instead of a guess.

pristabell.text: All nine are 10 ft (3 m) wide. Measure the length of the body without the hitch and pick the same length or the next one up. The price in this table is for one cover. The product page also offers two or three covers in a bundle, so if you have one RV, pick 1 pack there and the price stays the one you see here.
pristabell.fot: The shortest length is 18 ft and the width is 10 ft on every size. Is your rig shorter than 18 ft, or wider than 10 ft? Then this isn't the cover for you, and we'd rather say that here than in a return email.

punkter.rubrik: 1. Your RV isn't 18 ft. There is a size for a 39-footer too.
punkter.text: Several of you wrote that the store only offered one size, 18 × 10 ft. That's the bundle box on the product page: it opens with the first length at the top, and the size picker sits inside it, easy to miss. All nine lengths are in there, 18 to 44 ft, and the table above is the same list with a button for each one. Click your length and the product page opens with that size already picked. If you have one RV, choose 1 pack in the bundle box, and the price is the one in the table. Measure the body without the hitch. If your rig lands between two lengths, take the longer one.

punkter.rubrik: 2. Got an A/C unit on the roof? Here is what we know, and what we don't.
punkter.text: This is the most common question from the US, and our pictures are part of the problem: they show rigs with flat roofs, and not one of them has an A/C unit on top. Most American travel trailers and motorhomes carry a rooftop air conditioner and a couple of vent hoods, so you look at the pictures and see a cover that isn't made for your roof. Here is the honest state of it. The cover is 10 ft wide and comes in lengths up to 44 ft. It lies over the roof surface, and the straps latch under the edge of the body on all four sides. How it sits over an A/C unit, how much of the length the unit uses up, and whether you should go one size longer, we have asked the maker, and the answer goes right here the day it lands. Until then we won't guess for you. If you order anyway and it doesn't work over your A/C, the 90 days cover exactly that: get in touch and we arrange a return or refund.
punkter.knapp: See the cover → 90 days to try it

punkter.rubrik: 3. Those straps won't hold? Here is what they are made of.
punkter.text: Some of you have bought a roof cover before and had the straps give out: elastic cords that stretched, hooks that let go, marks left on the paint. So here is what the maker says about these straps, in their own words: woven webbing, not elastic, because elastic loses its stretch over time. There are straps on all four sides, adjustable, with hooks that latch under the edge of the body, and two extra reinforced straps in the box that go across the roof. On the paint, the maker says the straps will not damage it. That's their claim, and it's the one we pass on. What we won't give you is a wind rating, because there isn't one to quote, and we'd rather say nothing than make one up. If a strap ever fails on you, the 90 days are there for exactly that.
punkter.knapp: See the straps up close on the product page →

punkter.rubrik: 4. Doesn't a cover trap moisture? It can. Here is what to do about it.
punkter.text: A few of you asked whether a cover on a closed-up roof means condensation and mold, and you're right to ask. The fabric is waterproof, and a waterproof sheet lying flat on a roof doesn't move much air underneath. We're not going to tell you it breathes. What we're doing about it: a spacer that lifts the cover off the roof and lets air move under it is in the works. There's no date and no price yet, so it isn't on this page as a promise. Until it exists, lay something under the cover that keeps a gap, a couple of pool noodles or a strip of foam along the middle of the roof, so air can move. And give the roof a dry day before the cover goes on, not a wet one.
punkter.knapp: See the cover → nine sizes, one width

punkter.rubrik: 5. Why not the whole RV? Because you have to be able to get it on.
punkter.text: For that money I get a whole cover, a few of you wrote. Fair point, and we won't argue about the price of anyone else's cover. What a full-body cover asks of you is two people, a full length of fabric pulled over every corner without snagging, and a wrap that rubs against the sides every time the wind blows. That's the cover that tends to stay in the garage the second winter. This one covers the roof only, which is the surface where rain sits around the hatches and seams all winter. One person puts it on: unfold it on the roof, hook the straps under the edge on all four sides, pull the two reinforced straps across, done. The sides stay open. If what you want is the whole rig wrapped, this isn't it, and we'd rather you knew that now.
punkter.knapp: Cover the roof, not the whole rig →

punkter.rubrik: 6. Fifth wheel? Solar? Antenna? How to measure, and what we've asked the maker.
punkter.text: Fifth wheel: measure the main flat part of the roof and pick your length from that. Whether the cover also goes over the raised front above the hitch, we have asked the maker. Solar panels: the cover goes over them, so they're covered while it's on. If your batteries need the panels through the winter, this cover isn't the answer for that, and we won't pretend otherwise. Antenna, satellite dish, vent stacks, slide-out toppers: same honest answer as the A/C. We've asked, and the answers go on this page as they come in. What we can say today: the cover lies over the roof surface, the straps latch under the edge on all four sides, and the edge reaches over the top of the windows but never the lower half of the glass. How far down the sides it hangs depends on how wide your rig is, because the cover is 10 ft wide.

punkter.rubrik: 7. Anyone in the USA have one of these? Here is what you get if it doesn't fit.
punkter.text: One of you asked whether anyone in the US has one, because the reviews read like translations. They are translations: the reviews on the product page were written in other languages and the store translates them. There are no American reviews yet, and we won't make any up. So here is what you get instead of a testimonial. The full price list above, so the price for your length is on the table before you click, not in the cart. Free shipping to the US, 5 to 10 business days. And 90 days to try it: if the cover doesn't fit your rig, doesn't work over your A/C, or you simply change your mind, get in touch within 90 days and we arrange a return or refund. That's the deal, and it's written on the product page too.
punkter.knapp: Try it for 90 days → return or refund

fragor.rubrik: The short answers, for the rest of what you asked

lista.svar: Yes. Black 210D Oxford fabric, waterproof and sun-resistant, so water runs off instead of sitting at the hatches.

lista.fraga: Are there straps on the front and back, or just the sides?
lista.svar: All four sides. Woven webbing, adjustable, with hooks that latch under the edge of the body, plus two extra reinforced straps that go across the roof.

lista.fraga: Will it hold up in snow?
lista.svar: It's sold for winter storage, and the advice on the product page is to brush off heavy wet snow if it builds up, the same as you would without a cover. How much snow the fabric can carry, the maker hasn't given us a number for. We've asked.

lista.fraga: Black fabric in the sun. Doesn't it get hot?
lista.svar: The fabric is black and sun-resistant, and that's all we know about heat. We've asked the maker how hot it gets over acrylic windows before we say anything more.

lista.fraga: Can I put it on from a ladder, without walking on the roof?
lista.svar: One person puts it on: the folded fabric goes in the middle of the roof and unfolds toward the front and back, then the straps hook under the edge and the two long straps go across. Whether that works from a ladder alone on your rig, we've asked the maker for a video, and it goes here when we have it.

lista.fraga: Can I mix two sizes in one order?
lista.svar: Yes. In the bundle box you pick a size for each cover, so one for the trailer and one for the motorhome can go in the same order.

lista.fraga: What about my 13-footer, or a rig that's 12 ft wide?
lista.svar: Then it doesn't fit. The shortest length is 18 ft and the width is 10 ft on all nine sizes.
Shipping to the US is free, and delivery takes 5 to 10 business days.

lyckas.rubrik: So what do the people who order anyway do?
stycken: They measure the body without the hitch, pick the same length or the next one up in the table, and choose 1 pack if they have one rig. Then they use the 90 days as the test. The cover goes on before the first real rain, and if it doesn't sit right over the A/C, or the straps don't reach where they need to, it goes back. Nobody has to trust a translated review to find out.

What arrives is black 210D Oxford fabric, waterproof and sun-resistant, in your length and 10 ft wide, with woven webbing straps on all four sides and two extra reinforced straps for across the roof. It folds down to an armful-sized bundle when the season is over. Shipping to the US is free, delivery takes 5 to 10 business days, and the whole thing rests on one promise we can keep: 90 days, return or refund.

there are three things on this page we still don't know. How the cover sits over a rooftop A/C unit. Whether it goes over the raised front of a fifth wheel. And how much snow it carries. We've sent all three to the maker, and the answers go on this page when they come, not before.

Two things we do know, and they're not for everyone. The cover holds moisture under it the way any waterproof sheet does, so if you park somewhere damp and can't leave a gap under it, wait for the spacer. And it covers only the roof. If you want the sides and the wheels wrapped too, a full-body cover is the right product, just not this one.

And the price is what it is per length: $199 for 18 and 21 ft, up to $389 for 44 ft, and one cover costs what the table says. The product page also offers two or three covers in a bundle. If you have one rig, pick 1 pack.

You have 90 days to try it: if it doesn't fit your rig, doesn't work over the A/C, or you just change your mind, get in touch within 90 days and we arrange a return or refund. Shipping to the US is free.

lasbarhetstest.metod: Every paragraph read aloud as an American RV owner would hear it, the six points from /lagerrensning: each sentence picks up where the last one left off, mixed sentence length, at most one 'Not X. Y.' device per paragraph, one paragraph = one thought moving forward, words people use on the storage lot (rig, travel trailer, motorhome, fifth wheel, rooftop A/C, vent hoods, hitch, bundle box, storage lot), and the whole page read top to bottom as one person answering a comment thread in order: the table first (the loudest objection: 'only one size', 'Scam'), then 1 sizes → 2 A/C → 3 straps → 4 moisture → 5 the whole RV → 6 fifth wheel and the rest of the roof → 7 trust and the 90 days → the short answers → 'so what do they do' → 'I'll be honest' → risk-free.
lasbarhetstest.omskrivna_stycken: Hero: the first draft opened 'We read all your comments' — rewritten so the price objection (the reason people call it a scam) is the first word on the page. Point 2 (A/C): the first draft said 'because that's what we had to photograph' — untrue, the pictures are renders and supplier shots, so it now says what is checkable: 'not one of them has an A/C unit on top'. Point 3 (straps): 'plastic hooks' cut (the report says not to name the hook material until the maker answers); 'the maker says … in their own words' written so the claim is attributed, not ours. Point 4 (moisture): 'the people who cover boats do this' cut — unverifiable; the pool-noodle line kept because it's concrete and it's Axel's instruction ('lägg något under för luft'). Point 5: 'the door stays reachable' cut — the door is an open question in the report even though the product page says it stays clear; 'a lot of them end up in the garage' softened to 'tends to stay in the garage'. Point 7: the first draft said the reviews were 'written by customers in Europe' — only 'written in other languages and translated' is verifiable on the page ('Reviews in Other Languages'). 'I'll be honest' paragraph 3: 'no bundle is preselected on this page' cut — the product page does preselect a bundle until Axel decides A/B, so the paragraph now says what is true regardless: pick 1 pack if you have one rig. Numbers written as Americans say them: 39-footer, 32-footer, 10 ft, 5 to 10 business days (no dash ranges in prose).
lasbarhetstest.kvar_att_lyssna_pa: Point 5's heading 'Because you have to be able to get it on.' — the only heading that argues instead of pointing, and the one I'm least sure lands aloud; alternative: 'Why not the whole RV? One person can't get the whole RV on.' Also point 2 is the longest paragraph on the page (the A/C answer needs the honest 'we don't know' AND the safety net) — if it reads long on the phone, cut the sentence 'Until then we won't guess for you.'
